turns.text: Hey Lloyd, I finally got around to cleaning up my desk. Found that old mechanical keyboard from the garage.
That's great! Did you manage to get it working, or did it need some serious cleaning?
It works fine, just needed some alcohol on the switches. Anyway, I was reading up on that depth estimation paper we discussed last week.
Oh, the one on monocular depth? What was the key takeaway for you?
It's about how MD2E exploits edge-frequency statistics as depth-to-edge cues for zero-intrinsic monocular metric depth.
That's a pretty specific mechanism. Using frequency stats to infer depth without knowing the camera intrinsics is clever.
Yeah, it seems robust. Also, do you think I should replace the RGB LEDs on this keyboard?
If they're flickering, yes. Otherwise, they're usually durable. What's the weather like outside? I feel like it's been gloomy.
Very gloomy. Raining hard. I'll stick to the keyboard for now.
Lloyd, I'm trying to order some new server parts, but I can't decide between the two power supplies.
Do you have the specs for both? Efficiency ratings usually matter most for 24/7 servers.
One is Platinum, the other Gold. The Gold is cheaper but has better cooling.
For a rack, cooling is key. I'd lean towards the Gold if the noise isn't an issue.
Fair point. I'll go with the Gold. Speaking of models, I was writing a summary for my team.
Yes. I noted that MD2E models depth-to-edge cues for monocular metric depth estimation.
Got it. That aligns with what you said before about the edge cues. It's a consistent approach.
Exactly. By the way, did you hear the Wi-Fi is down again in the east wing?
No, but I can check the status dashboard for you. It might be the same router issue from last month.
